supporting_observations.claim: The alerted failures are repeated attempts for svc-routes from FILE-COP-01, with roughly one-minute spacing from 13:36 through 13:51 UTC. The 4625 records report bad-password status 0xc000006a; examples include the first, middle, and last failures in this run.

The corresponding domain-controller validation events identify FILE-COP-01 as the workstation and report the same bad-password status; the Kerberos pre-authentication failures also originate from the same internal address shown on the FILE-COP-01 events.

The pattern is consistent with the supplied context that svc-routes re-authenticates every minute and its password was scheduled for rotation at 13:30 UTC; recurring bad-password attempts after a rotation are plausibly explained by the job continuing to use a stale credential.

At 14:07 UTC, a SYSTEM-context PowerShell process on FILE-COP-01 used explicit credentials for svc-routes against DC-COP-01. This is consistent with the supplied context that the RouteSync job must be updated manually, though the event alone does not establish that an update succeeded.

known_telemetry_limitations: The provided records show failed authentications and a later explicit-credential-use event, but do not show whether the 14:07 credential use succeeded or whether the RouteSync job was successfully updated (T122-00001 through T122-00036).

The authentication records identify FILE-COP-01 and LSASS as the logon source/process, but do not identify the specific RouteSync executable or job instance responsible for each attempt (T122-00001 through T122-00035).
claims_not_established: Whether the 14:07 PowerShell event completed a legitimate password update or was followed by successful svc-routes authentication.
Whether any actor or process other than the scheduled RouteSync job caused the failures.
